key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces, reducing interfacial recombination and enabling 25.86% power conversion efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface stoichiometry offers a route to improved electron extraction into C60 in methylammonium-free solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to probe iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to electronic character, electron extraction, and recombination.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% device efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term stability and manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the surface treatment are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
